meta.title_plain: How a boy who practised in an empty pool won 24 Grand Slams
meta.teaser: Novak Djokovic kept training through hard times and became tennis's record Grand Slam winner.

page.title: How a boy who practised in an empty pool won 24 Grand Slams
page.bigIdea: Novak Djokovic kept practising when everything around him was hard. That steady work made him the record Grand Slam winner in men's tennis.

cards.title: A mini-racket at four
cards.front: Novak was born in 1987 in Belgrade, Serbia.
cards.back: At age 4, his parents gave him a mini-racket and a soft foam ball. His family ran a pizza place near tennis courts in the mountains.
cards.tryit: Find the oldest racket or ball in your house. Hit 30 easy shots with it.

cards.title: The coach on the mountain
cards.front: At 6, Novak joined a tennis camp on Mount Kopaonik.
cards.back: Coach Jelena Genčić spotted his talent and coached him for about six years. He said she helped shape his mind as a person and a player.
cards.tryit: Write down one thing a coach taught you that you still use today.

cards.title: Tennis in a swimming pool
cards.front: In 1999, Serbia was hit by bombing during a war.
cards.back: Times were scary and hard, but Novak kept training. At one point he practised inside an empty swimming pool turned into a tennis court.
cards.tryit: Practise in a small space today: 20 soft volleys against a wall, no big swings.

cards.title: Leaving home at twelve
cards.front: In 1999, Novak moved to a tennis academy in Germany.
cards.back: He was about 12 and stayed four years at coach Niki Pilić's academy. It was like leaving your village to train, like Luffy setting sail.
cards.tryit: Plan one week of training: write which day you'll work on serves, volleys and fitness.

cards.title: Records on records
cards.front: In 2008, at 20, he won his first Grand Slam.
cards.back: It was the Australian Open. Since then he has won 24 Grand Slams, spent 428 weeks at No. 1, and won Olympic gold in 2024.
cards.tryit: Set a 'record' of your own: count your longest rally with a friend, then try to beat it.

quiz.q: Where did Novak once practise during the hard times of 1999?
quiz.hint: Look at card 3. It was a place that usually has water.
quiz.why: He trained in a disused pool that had been turned into a tennis court.

quiz.q: Who spotted Novak's talent at a mountain camp?
quiz.hint: She coached him for about six years, starting when he was 6.
quiz.why: Jelena Genčić ran the camp on Mount Kopaonik and coached him for years.

quiz.q: Which Grand Slam has Novak won a record 10 times?
quiz.hint: It was also his very first Grand Slam title, in 2008.
quiz.why: He won his first Slam in Melbourne in 2008 and has won it 10 times.

quiz.q: What did Novak do at about age 12?
opts: Moved to an academy in Germany
quiz.hint: Think about card 4 and the word 'leaving'.
quiz.why: He moved to Niki Pilić's academy in Germany and trained there for four years.

page.think: Novak kept training even when life around him was tough. What is one thing that sometimes stops you from practising, and how could you still do a little anyway?
